# readmit <img src="man/figures/logo.png" align="right" height="138" alt="" />

<!-- badges: start -->
[![CRAN Status](https://www.r-pkg.org/badges/version/readmit)](https://cran.r-project.org/package=readmit)
![CRAN\_Download\_Counter](http://cranlogs.r-pkg.org/badges/grand-total/readmit)
[![Codecov test coverage](https://codecov.io/gh/centralstatz/readmit/graph/badge.svg)](https://app.codecov.io/gh/centralstatz/readmit)
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/centralstatz/readmit/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/centralstatz/readmit/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)

`readmit` creates editable, user-owned Readmission Risk Pool (RRP) projects.
Each project includes configuration, source-mapping and risk-provider scripts,
branding, and its own Shiny application. Persistent history can be initialized
explicitly, `rrp_run()` retains completed assessments, and status and history
inspection are available. `rrp_refresh_products()` writes analytical CSVs from
retained history; populated app views are a later development stage.

## Create and open a project

After installing `readmit`, create a project at a new destination:

```r
library(readmit)

project <- rrp_project_init(
  path = "my-rrp-project",
  project_id = "my-project"
)

rrp_project_validate(project)
```

The path is relative to your current working directory unless you supply an
absolute path. Its parent directory must already exist, and the destination
must not exist, even as an empty directory. The generated files belong to you:
edit `rrp-project.dcf`, `rrp-authoring.dcf`, `_brand.yml`,
`R/produce-canonical.R`, and `R/calculate-risk.R` for your project.
`rrp_project_validate()` checks that the configuration and both authoring
functions load; it does not run them. Both generated functions begin as
deliberate stubs, so the untouched project passes this structural check.
Implement the source mapper to return the canonical discharge episodes and
terminal events described in the project README, and implement the risk
provider for eligible episodes. Validate again after editing. Validation checks
that the scripts load; it does not establish that their data or predictions will
work during a run.

Then initialize persistent history and run at an explicit UTC analytical time:

```r
rrp_state_init(project)
assessment <- rrp_run(
  project, as.POSIXct("2026-01-10 12:00:00", tz = "UTC")
)
rrp_project_status(project)
rrp_inspect_history(project, run_id = assessment$run_id)
rrp_refresh_products(project)
```

This creates empty `state/history.duckdb` tables in the project and refuses to
overwrite existing state. State initialization does not run either authoring
function. Each `rrp_run()` call obtains canonical facts, assesses eligible
episodes through the provider, and atomically appends the completed run and its
episode outcomes. It returns the run ID and accepted, failed, and ineligible
counts. `rrp_project_status()` also works before state initialization;
`rrp_inspect_history()` requires state. Both read retained information without
sourcing your scripts. A provider failure is retained for its episode while
other eligible episodes continue. Completed runs append history; later event
knowledge does not rewrite earlier results. After at least one completed run,
`rrp_refresh_products()` reads history and writes
`state/products/current-remaining-risk.csv`,
`remaining-risk-trajectory.csv`, and `operational-scope-summary.csv`. It selects
the run with the greatest analytical time, which may differ from the most
recently executed run. Supply the complete relevant discharge population for
operational assessments: a later partial run replaces the earlier population
in current products. The package determines clinical eligibility. Eligible
provider-failure episodes stay in the current-risk file with a missing
probability; earlier estimates are not substituted. Refresh does not rerun your
scripts, change history, or edit the app. The three-file replacement is staged
but is not fully atomic if a filesystem error occurs during final replacement.

The application uses `shiny`, `bslib`, and `yaml` in the environment where it
runs. Install them there, then launch the app directly from the same working
directory used in the example:

```r
install.packages(c("shiny", "bslib", "yaml"))
shiny::runApp("my-rrp-project/app")
```

The app opens with Current Risk Pool and Overview views. Its current empty
states remain until populated product views are implemented in a later stage.
